dedupe_keys.name: modbus normal and malicious network traffic zero swarm factory i o captures

description: This deposit holds network traces from a simulated factory built in Factory I/O and controlled over Modbus: two packet captures of normal operation, one of a man-in-the-middle and flooding attack and one of an Nmap probe attack. The Zenodo page gives the creators as Lazaridis and Mpatziakas and the keywords cybersecurity, IIoT and network traffic; the file names tie it to the Zero-SWARM project. Version 1.0 was published on 25 March 2025 as four downloadable PCAP files of about 270 MB in total, free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is one laboratory testbed, not a real plant, so there is no geographic coverage. Caveats: the page does not describe the factory scene, the number of devices, the capture duration or any labels inside the files, so these are not stated on the page read, and attack traffic is separated only by file. For simulation it supports training and testing intrusion detection for industrial control networks and building cyber-attack scenarios into manufacturing and infrastructure digital twins, where a compromised controller stops a production line. Related catalogue records include the ICS SCADA cyber kit testbed traffic data and the HELICS co-simulation platform.
